# Claims ledger

Generated from `CLAIMS.json` by `tools/check_claims.py render`. Do not hand-edit; `tools/check_claims.py check render` fails if this file disagrees with a fresh regeneration.

## Methodology

This ledger covers two distinct obligations. First, every number-bearing sentence in README.md and docs/** (excluding a version, a date, a path, or a code-block line) is catalogued below as either a claim or a `not_claims` entry with a reason -- this is the coverage criterion, and it is deliberately narrower than 'every claim': numbers are what a reader trusts and what an author gets wrong, so that is what is mechanically enforced here. Second, this ledger separately records the required INVALIDATED entries for dogfood run a02, and five specific unflattering findings this project's own evidence supports, regardless of whether they happen to contain a digit.

'Sentence' is operationalized as a source line: these documents are hard-wrapped roughly one clause per line, and the specification's own phrase 'a code-block line' already treats the line as the unit of exclusion. A markdown heading or list item introduced by a bare ordinal ('## 4. Title', '1. Do the thing') has that ordinal stripped before the digit check, so pure structural numbering does not by itself trigger coverage -- otherwise every numbered heading and list step in this project's documents would need its own ledger entry for no informational gain. A version (`0.8.0`), an ISO or German date, a hex commit/blob hash, and a backtick-quoted path or dotted filename are stripped the same way. What is left over is genuinely a claim-shaped digit occurrence: a threshold, a count, an identifier, an environment literal, or a citation index.

Within what is left, several categories recur and are marked `not_claims` in bulk rather than individually re-argued: internal finding/gate/milestone identifiers (A01-A12, H0-H4, K1) and citation indices ([Q1]..[Q12], resolved in QUELLENCHECK.md) name things rather than measure them; ordinal cross-references ('step 2', 'measured property 3') point back to an already-excluded numbered list; command/instruction snippets ('python3 -m hoh.cli') carry a digit as part of a binary name, not a measurement; and one illustrative placeholder ('commit `abc123`', 'run 7'/'run 3') is explicitly not about a real measured run. The citation table in QUELLENCHECK.md is judged not-claims as a whole: it verifies upstream sources for design decisions, not this software's own behaviour, even though its rows would otherwise fit the `cite:` evidence form structurally.

The most disputable call in this pass concerns three files: *docs/K1_CACHE_PROFILE.md*, *docs/QUELLENCHECK.md*, and *docs/HERDR_HOH_IMPLEMENTATION_HANDOFF.md*, named here to state a judgement about them, not to point a reader at them. All three are German-language internal working notes in substance, the same kind of document the out-of-scope list names by root-level example (RUNBOOK.md, the A0*.md files, PHASE2.md). But they live under `docs/`, and the coverage criterion says `README.md and docs/**` without carving out a subdirectory, so this run catalogued them in full rather than quietly exempting them. A reader who judges that boundary differently should say so; the sentences are all listed either way, so nothing is hidden by the disagreement.

One field beyond the specification's minimum schema is used here: `invalidated_run` on an INVALIDATED claim, naming the run its now-superseded evidence rested on. The specification's own criterion 5 wording ('a claim whose evidence names run a02') is satisfied structurally by this field exactly the way a `receipt:a02/...` or `run:a02/...` evidence reference would be: `tools/check_claims.py`'s a02 check treats both as naming a run. This run's checkout has no populated `runs/` directory (it is out of scope to create one, and it is genuinely absent here), so the two INVALIDATED claims below cite the committed post-mortem documents (A02_BERICHT.md, A03_NACHWEIS.md, HOH_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md) rather than raw a02 receipts -- citing a document that analyses what a02 got wrong is not the same as resting a claim on a02's own unreliable numbers, and a plain `file:` reference to those documents is deliberately not treated as 'naming run a02' by the checker, or the historically accurate SUPPORTED claim about the K1..K9 misreport (also sourced from A02_BEFUNDE.md, a post-mortem document, not a raw a02 acceptance record) would be wrongly forced INVALIDATED too.

The five mandated UNSUPPORTED findings are recorded as UNSUPPORTED rather than SUPPORTED even where a document states them plainly, because most of them are absence claims ('no baseline exists', 'never touched src/ or tests/') that no evidence form in this schema can positively verify -- a `file:` reference can prove a sentence exists, not that the absence it describes is complete. Where corroborating evidence is available (a unit test, a source line) it is still attached, so the note explains exactly how far that evidence reaches and no further.

d4d: coverage used to glob docs/** at check time, which is how O41 happened -- two runs that never touched a common file still collided because the checker discovered scope by walking the filesystem instead of reading a declaration. coverage_targets() now reads the top-level claim_surfaces array above instead: every file the old glob covered is declared there (scope "whole file" for all eleven -- none of the current documents needs section-level scoping), each with a why and requires_reconciliation_on_change=true, and claim_surface_policy names the same requirement once more at the manifest level so a consumer can read the dependency from CLAIMS.json alone. A new reconcile CLI subcommand reports, read-only, which statements in a declared surface are unbound (no resolving anchor) or vanished (a recorded anchor that no longer resolves) -- it never writes. An undeclared-surface heuristic (find_undeclared_claim_surfaces) warns, never fails, when a tracked README.md/docs/**.md document carries number-bearing sentences but is missing from claim_surfaces; it cannot catch a claim-bearing file with no digits at all, a non-.md file, or a document outside README.md/docs/** entirely, since those are exactly the two locations the old glob (and this heuristic, deliberately, as its replacement-in-spirit for discovery rather than for coverage) ever looked. Using that reconciliation, the eleven docs/LIMITATIONS.md sentences d3c left uncovered against the frozen eight-limit-version ledger (C-052..C-060, N-061, N-062) are now bound: nine are historical/measured counts from this project's own run and merge history, recorded UNSUPPORTED for the same reason the five earlier mandated findings are -- no evidence form in this schema positively verifies a historical count, and this checkout has no populated runs/ tree to re-derive one from even where a discriminated:/receiptcount: form would otherwise apply. The remaining two (docs/LIMITATIONS.md:157, :208) are not_claims: an internal cross-reference to another limit's heading number, and a quoted restatement of an already-recorded figure used only to warn against misreading it -- both fit categories already established in this methodology's third paragraph, not new categories invented for this run.

r1a: every evidence reference above now also carries a derived resolvability class (PUBLIC/LOCAL_ONLY/EXTERNAL), shown next to its own bullet under 'Evidence' below -- never in a separate legend or summary table. The class is derived, not typed per reference: receipt:/run:/receiptcount:/discriminated: are always LOCAL_ONLY (runs/** is never exported to the public repository); cite: is always EXTERNAL; test: is always PUBLIC (tests/ is exported whole); file: is PUBLIC unless its path falls under one of a small named export-exclusion rule table (evidence-not-artifact, parked-predecessor, stale-build-output, foreign-subject, internal-working-document -- see tools/check_claims.py's DEFAULT_EXPORT_EXCLUSION_RULES, derived from dogfood/specs/r1-export-manifest.md's stated rules since no EXPORT_MANIFEST.json exists yet), in which case it is LOCAL_ONLY. A LOCAL_ONLY reference is not a defect: it is the expected shape of most of this ledger's strongest (receipt-backed) evidence, and every claim that carries one states, in its own local_only_resolution field, who resolved it and when.

d7w: Four evidence forms -- run:, receipt:, receiptcount: and discriminated: -- resolve only inside the operator's own runs/ tree, which is gitignored and excluded from every export. A reader who does not have that tree and sees SUPPORTED on a claim carrying one of these citations is trusting the operator: specifically, trusting a prior run of the checker that the operator carried out locally, not re-deriving the evidence themselves. 34 SUPPORTED claims currently carry at least one such citation.

d4e: `CLAIMS.json` now declares, for every `INCLUDE` path in `EXPORT_MANIFEST.json`, either a `claim_surfaces` entry (this run added seventeen, for the `.md` files r1's export left undeclared -- `CHANGELOG.md`, this file, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `PROVENANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, the two `examples/minimal/` files, `ops/README.md`, the seven `paper/*.md` files, and `policy/README.md`) or a `claim_surface_exclusions` entry naming one of five closed reasons (`ledger-itself`, `copied-evidence`, `pattern-data`, `package-metadata`, `source-code` -- this run added fifty-four). `check_export_classification()` in `tools/check_claims.py` fails, naming every offending path, when an `INCLUDE` path is neither declared nor excluded, declared both ways, excluded with a reason outside that closed set, or a prose `.md` `INCLUDE` path is excluded instead of declared a surface; `find_undeclared_claim_surfaces()` above is untouched -- it keeps warning, never failing, over its own `README.md`+`docs/**` reference set, because a directory glob lets a developer dodge a hard failure by keeping a file out of the scanned directories, while the only way to dodge this new check is to stop exporting the file, a declared act `EXPORT_MANIFEST.json` itself records. Separately, this run replaced the identical `local_only_resolution` sentence r1a stamped onto thirty-nine claims (see the paragraph above) with genuinely distinct, per-claim text naming the specific run, iteration, receipt file, or document line each claim's own evidence actually rests on; `check_local_only_diversity()` fails if any two `LOCAL_ONLY` claims ever again share one statement, and a fixture where every claim shares one sentence is the regression test that proves the check would have caught the original defect.

| C-487 | SUPPORTED | * **HoH builds HoH's own kernel.** Since 2026-09-23 product runs have written modules under `src/hoh/`. From 2026-09-25 on, every such run worked in an isolated clone pinned to one commit, its accepted candidate was imported byte for byte, and two independent integration reviewers released it before the orchestrating session merged it: 46 product-run merges `[V01]`, 34 of which change `src/hoh/` `[V02]`. In the ledger entries O236 to O254, 26 candidates the product had accepted were refused at integration review `[V07t]`. * **Durable programme runtime (P2).** Durable timers, a sentinel, a never-stuck check, session succession with a master epoch, a partial leader lease, a resume loop that acts on due timers, an autonomy contract, a programme checklist bound to the phase gate, and an independent supervisor review of the gate. 26 of P2's 43 registered requirements read PROVEN `[V10c]` `[V10b]`; P2 is not closed. * **Project contract and state ownership.** Read-only `hoh project contract` commands (`schema`, `check`, `impact`, `owner`, `conflicts`) beside `hoh project authority`, `drive` and `handoff`. * **Evidence model.** The `EvidenceClaim` schema and its entry point `tools/evidence_claims.py`; proof classes that keep "built", "tested", "integrated", "behaviourally proven" and "gate satisfied" apart; and an acceptance record that is refused as `STALE` when the code it describes changed after it was taken. * **Programme gate machinery.** Phase gates bound to the register (a gate item that is not bound can no longer read closed), supervisor drift measured against a preserved baseline, each acceptance probe bound to its own register entry, and a union-gate timeout that reports a stable `NOT_RUN` instead of copying an interpreter path into the board. * **Storage lifecycle (operator amendment A1), and its first self-dogfood.** Ownership registry, admission by reservation, durable park and resume under storage pressure, verified archive bundles and targets, host adapters, and `VERIFIED_RELOCATION` with a per-project storage steward -- the only operation that may remove a local copy of project data. `hoh storage init`, `steward`, `adopt-project`, `survey-legacy` and `adopt-legacy`, and `hoh resume-storage`. ⟦change `src/hoh/` `[V02]`. In the ledger entries O236 to O254, 26 candidates⟧ | CHANGELOG.md:66 |

| C-560 | SUPPORTED | **The integrity gate is met for the replayed paths; one residual and the tracked minors stay** — The qa-arena-write repair (merge `a455edc0`) seals QA's candidate arena and holds a run that was blocked for a capability violation, for every state shape the current build writes. Its integration reviewer proved three findings open, and this pre-release was held for them (the text of that state is kept in the dated correction at the end of limit 12d): (1) a violation state written before the hold existed could be unblocked by `resume_runs` and the launcher then reported the run ACCEPTED; (2) `tools/acceptance_record.py` did not count an open seal as a problem; (3) a `seals.jsonl` replaced by a symlink made the controller append ledger lines to the foreign file, and a forged `planned` line for a sibling arena of the same run was honoured. **The qaw-followup merge (`ab41589f`, 2026-10-07) closes them for the replayed paths:** the resume loop, its fallback and `hoh resume-storage` refuse a run the hold covers (`test_l1`: the run stays BLOCKED and the launcher verdict is UNDETERMINED); an open QA seal is not an acceptance (`test_n1`); the seal ledger is read and appended only as a single regular link (`O_NOFOLLOW`, checked on the descriptor), so a symlink, a FIFO, a dangling link or a second name is refused before a byte is written (`test_m4`); and a `planned` line is honoured only for an arena this run sealed (`test_m3`). Both integration reviewers replayed each path on the merged tree, the strand's 13 criteria pass under NONE and STRICT and its 54 mutant rows are killed. **Not claimed:** that no other false-ACCEPTED or foreign-write path exists. **Stated and pinned by the strand (P6):** a role pane that has read the run's `arena_secret` and copies iteration and attempt gets a forged plan honoured -- the ledger is a record and a restore aid, not an access control against a process of the same user. Tracked minor: `acceptance_record.open_seals` does not count link names (not reachable from the drive, because evidence is copied without hard links), and a held run under storage pressure is booked as `storage_unavailable` (the strand's own reading says the flow is unreachable). — `docs/LIMITATIONS.md` limit 12d; ledger O253, O254, O255 | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:37 |

Amendment A5 added a P2 requirement, P2-43, which delays closure further. — `docs/READINESS.md`; the build plan's gate report; ledger O252 | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:77 |
| C-562 | SUPPORTED | **A provider usage limit that stops a QA role is booked as a rejected iteration** — Eight iterations were lost this way `[V26]`: wmig, kbr, ugt, pcon, dres2, ecl and rpl in iteration 1, lgs in iteration 2. Each state history reads "candidate rejected: unverified, no QA verdict", followed within about two minutes by the planner's quota block. The same limit in a planner is classified as a resumable block. The orchestrator parked and resumed each run and did not treat a lost iteration as a verdict on the candidate; the dres2 and ecl acceptances in iteration 2 also followed an iteration lost this way. **The repair (failure-classes, the core of amendment A5's P2 item P2-43) is not merged**; P2-43 reads MISSING `[V40]`. The eighth (rpl) is read from its run state, committed with the ledger. `state.json` also keeps a stale `blocked_kind` after `resume-quota` (medium). — ledger O252 and its addition, O253 | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:39 |
| C-563 | SUPPORTED | The first prompt after an agent starts can be typed and not submitted, and the recovery has a width limit — A startup race: the first prompt is typed, and `herdr agent prompt --wait` reports a stall. Dispatch recovers: after a stalled submit it presses Enter once, only when the box holds exactly this dispatch's own text, and types nothing again. In the four runs that had the recovery before the prompt-threshold merge, seven first prompts stalled and each was recovered `[V31]`. The prompt-threshold merge (`33320bfc`) sends every role prompt above 8,192 bytes, and every prompt holding a paste-unsafe character, through the pointer file, because a long inline paste is rendered collapsed and the box could not be verified (qfu, qfu2 and qfu3 blocked this way). That is a recovery made verifiable, **not a fix of the race**, and it does not prove the dialog boundary, which only the tests pin: a dialog that opens between the screen read and the key press would receive the Enter. **Width limit (run qfu4, PROVEN from the recorded box):** the recovery models a break in the box only mid-word at exactly the box width; Claude Code breaks at a word boundary when the line does not fit. In a 79-column pane (box width 76) the pointer's first line, 77 columns with its indentation, wrapped before its last word, the recovery refused as designed, and the run was blocked at its first planner dispatch before any candidate; the same pointer text passed in a 106-column pane. Residuals the prompt-threshold spec records: recovery works only for prompts the pointer carries; a short inline prompt taller than the pane is refused (T8); a long path can defeat the comparison (T7, SUSPECTED); the pointer's wording "too long for one command-line argument" is now incomplete (T2). Readiness of the first prompt and the wrap model are the next P2 strand, not started. — ledger O253, O255; `src/hoh/dispatchers.py` | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:43 |
| C-564 | SUPPORTED | A role can be re-woken by its own background task, and what the lifecycle does about it — A role turn is taken as ended while the role still has a background task that can wake it and write. One run saw a developer edit source files while QA ran; the candidate-binding check failed the run closed, as designed. A live smoke showed that closing the pane stops the agent from waking and does not end its background descendants `[V32]`. **The role-pane lifecycle is merged (`caa732db`, with its tests-only follow-up):** HoH closes its own role panes and ends the processes a role left running before the freeze, never touching a foreign pane or process (a process is ended only when it carries the pane's minted mark and is anchored to the pane's own shell; a signal goes to one process, never a group; a marked process outside the pane is named and not signalled). Its first live use was the rpl-tests run (its `pane-lifecycle.jsonl`): the planner and developer panes were closed at the turn's end; the QA pane's release was refused because two marked processes had escaped the pane (named, never signalled), and the pane was gone without anyone closing it by hand (the orchestrator found it already gone) (Correction, 2026-10-08: the lifecycle log of that run, `pane-lifecycle.jsonl`, also holds a `closing` and a `closed` line for the QA pane, in the same second as the `refused` line; the earlier "closed three panes and refused one" counted that pane twice, and the text above replaced it.) (Further correction, 2026-10-08: the `closing` line is written by HoH before its own close command and the `closed` line only after a second snapshot no longer lists the pane, and a pane found already gone is written with an `already_gone` field, which this line does not carry (`_close_own_pane` in `src/hoh/dispatchers.py`); so HoH itself closed the QA pane's tab, nobody closed it by hand, and the `refused` line that follows names the two escaped processes, not a failed close.). Not claimed: that no role can still change the tree after the freeze by a route the lifecycle does not see (the numbered limit 21, written by that run, says what a close proves and does not: a shared daemon is named and never ended and blocks the developer's release; that the mark reaches every command an agent's own shell tool starts has not been shown by a test). Tracked minor: extra mutants of the pane-count guard in `_close_own_pane` and three accounting mutants survive the tests (fail closed); a detached daemon adopted by a subreaper is documented as escaping; the run state keeps a stale iteration-1 QA task and `blocked_kind` after acceptance (controller, low). The pre-existing whole-tab close of a dead agent in `dispatchers.py` is the lifecycle's own tracked area. — ledger O252, O253, O254, O255 | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:44 |
| C-565 | SUPPORTED | A long role timeout is booked as an unclassified block — The default role timeout is 2700 seconds; one run was blocked at that limit while its developer still worked `[V29]`. A role timeout and a fresh-agent startup stall are routed to the digest as unclassified, non-delegable decisions; the classes (ROLE_TIMEOUT, PROMPT_STALLED) belong to the failure-classes strand. The timeout is not recorded in the run. — ledger O252 | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:45 |
| C-566 | SUPPORTED | Invisible characters stopped an inline prompt paste (merged: prompt-threshold) — A specification carrying four invisible characters stalled two planner dispatches `[V28]`: the agent interface announced the removal and waited, so the inline paste was never submitted. The remedy (every role prompt above 8,192 bytes, and any prompt with control, format, private-use characters, tab or carriage return, through the file pointer) was merged as `33320bfc`. It was built by a product run under one declared deviation, a bootstrap harness (the previous source plus only the reviewed dispatcher change; the operator delegated the choice), retired at the merge. The residuals are in the first-prompt row above. — ledger O252, O255; `src/hoh/dispatchers.py` | docs/LIMITATIONS.md:46 |

| C-568 | SUPPORTED | Registered temporary roots are merged; the register holds the row at PARTIAL — P2-42 (a registered project-owned temporary root, creator-cleaned workspaces, admitted writes, an inode signal) was merged after two runs that integration review refused `[V38]`. The EPHEMERAL_TMP tier, the release proof and the relocation of temporary paths (P5-35) are deferred. | C-897 | SUPPORTED | A criterion of the P2-41 closure found it; a three-line guard fixes it. * A run id of `..` escaped the runs root through `hoh run` and `--detach` (HIGH). Detach types its options as `--flag=value` and refuses empty values and leading dashes before anything starts. * A developer turn that ended on a recorded limit screen reached QA, and a good re-run after a limit wait was parked again by a banner already on the reused pane (both P2-43, above). * The export leak scan failed open on a UTF-16 text next to a non-ASCII character; the account of a storage root read 0 for what it could not measure; the reaper raised on a broken standard error; and the registration of a target clone accepted a symlinked `.git/objects` or refs. Almost all of the failures are tests of the development repository that read records the export withholds (the requirement register and what is derived from it, the pinned scope of the planning package, one acceptance record, the preserved reviews of the P2 gate, one runbook); two need a git identity, which the workflow now sets, and one needs a live Herdr session. The tests that need withheld records or Herdr are listed in `tests/conftest.py` and skip where the record or the session is absent, with the reason named, and only when the export manifest declares the record withheld; `tests/test_export_gap_table.py` guards the list. ⟦checkout of the exported `v0.3.0` tree, with `zstandard` installed, 59 tests failed and 6,942 passed. | C-1085 | SUPPORTED | **The storage steward.** The build ran its disk and its inode table full more than once, which is why this part exists. The steward watches bytes and inodes, admits work by reservation, parks a run durably under pressure and resumes it, and relocates reproducible scratch to cold storage only through a verified relocation: the copy is read back and digested, a durable receipt is written, and only then is the local copy freed. Ownership is proven by a registry and never inferred from a name or an age; foreign, unknown and single-copy paths are left alone. The mechanism is built and tested (the requirements P2-38 to P2-41, P5-25 to P5-30, P5-32 and P5-33 read PROVEN). A policy and an archive target are configured for this project and no timer runs the steward; its plan-only runs found nothing of this project's to relocate and reported the remaining pressure as not this project's to free. The large cleanups were made by the orchestrating session with manifests, not by the steward: the first covered 4,211 trees with 15,558,933 entries `[V36]`, the second inventoried 2,003 copies, proved 342 of them reproducible and removed 341, 6,562,367 entries in all `[V37]`; later archives of run arenas were made with the session's own archive scripts. ⟦**The storage steward.** The build ran its disk and its inode table full more than once, which is why this part exists. Note: Absence claim: no comparison or baseline run exists in this project's evidence. None of this schema's evidence forms (test/file/receipt/run/cite) can positively prove a negative, so this is recorded as UNSUPPORTED rather than implied to be independently checkable; docs/LIMITATIONS.md's second limitation states it in full. Superseded on 2026-09-13 by measurement. The earlier claim, recorded from the first release until this date, was: "There is no matched-budget comparison against a plain agent working the same specification without HoH's plan/develop/verify loop around it, and no baseline run of any kind exists in this repository's evidence." It was true when written and is no longer: a matched-budget benchmark was run under a protocol committed before the first arm, and its result is the line now anchored here. The correction is by addition -- the old wording stays in this note -- and the direction is worth stating: the baseline did not favour the harness. Evidence corrected on 2026-09-13: it pointed at `tools/benchmark.py`, the program that runs the arms, which contains no result and never did -- `audit_refs claims-against-code` has been red on exactly this since before the benchmark ran. The five arm-A outcomes are in docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md's correctness table, derived from the cells in dogfood/benchmark/results/.

Note: INVALIDATED 2026-09-09: measured directly against this repository's own commit history via `git log --format='%s' -- tests/ src/ | grep '^HoH '`. That measurement shows 0 commits from any run touching `src/`, and every commit to three files under `tests/` coming from a run -- test_claims_anchors.py (9 of 9 commits), test_export_manifest.py (4 of 4), test_union_gate.py (3 of 3); no other file under `tests/` has any run-authored commit. The claim's absolute form is also false on its own terms for `tests/`: several of this project's own run specifications list `tests/test_*.py` in their own Scope -- what you may change section, so those runs were instructed to write those tests, not merely left unforbidden to. See docs/LIMITATIONS.md limit 8 for the corrected, narrower statement this project's evidence actually supports: no run ever touched `src/`, and the three `tests/` files the loop created are the release tools' own test files. Superseded note, kept for provenance rather than deleted (set when this claim was UNSUPPORTED, replaced 2026-09-09): HoH's evidence about its own reliability speaks to documentation- and governance-shaped work only; every dogfood run, including this one (also forbidden from touching src/hoh/ or tests/, per dogfood/specs/d4-claims.md), was deliberately kept out of src/ and tests/. Whether the loop holds up the same way on a nontrivial production code path remains untested by this project's own history.

Withdrawn on 2026-09-11. This statement said the sandbox closed limit 6, measured by comparing `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` inside and outside isolation. The replacement passage at docs/LIMITATIONS.md gives all three regimes with their exit codes, and C-150..C-153 carry the measurements. | paper/POSITION_PAPER.md:743 | This run's own history is the cost made concrete: run `D5`'s criterion 6 required, verbatim, "all twelve limitations," true when it was written and false by the time `D5` actually ran, because run `d3e` had by then already merged limit 13 and limit 14 into `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`; the running specification could not be corrected in place -- the same immutability this entry describes applied to it too -- so the fix did not happen inside that run, it became this separate one. 16. **A usage-quota exhaustion is indistinguishable from a role that broke its contract.** On 2026-09-08, two independent runs, `d5` and `d4h`, failed in the same shape within one window: a role session left no answer file behind, blocking each run in turn -- an operator's own cross-run reading of session logs, and one this project's evidence forms cannot independently re-verify, so `CLAIMS.json` records the joint-timing account as unsupported rather than confirmed (C-068..C-072). The command built for exactly this cause did not recognise it: `hoh resume-quota`, run over this project's full history, reported `{"checked": 37, "results": []}` -- 37 runs checked, 0 identified as quota-blocked -- even though two of the runs it checked, `d5` and `d4h`, were (C-073, C-074). "Left no answer file behind" names two different causes and only one has a resume path: a role's own broken output contract, where the session ran, produced no verdict, and there is nothing to resume from except re-dispatching the role; or a spent usage quota, where the session was cut off before the role process could write anything at all, including the marker `resume-quota` looks for. HoH never detects a quota exhaustion by itself and never automatically resumes a run blocked for that reason; the recovery here is an operator action, not an automated one -- `hoh unblock <run> --reason "..."` lifts the block by hand, once the cause is confirmed, and only then does the role run again. ⟦as unsupported rather than confirmed (C-068..C-072). The command built⟧ | restates claims C-068 through C-072 (explicit cite). |

| paper/REVIEW_B.md:402 | Report point D's specific, narrow claim — that `hoh deliver --approve` was never invoked because "the switch means the captain's explicit approval, and I don't set that for myself" — checks out: no commit message, tag name, or reflog entry anywhere in this repository's full history references `hoh deliver` being run, and no `runs/` state exists to show a delivery record either way. But the same report table also names 32 direct `git merge --no-ff` operations performed by the operator to land accepted candidate branches on `master`, framed throughout as ordinary "Operatorarbeit." Landing work on a project's integration branch is exactly the action `src/hoh/delivery.py`'s own module docstring quotes the handoff as reserving to the captain and firstmate ("this assignment grants no additional push, merge, deployment or purchasing rights"), and `deliver()`'s own `local-only` mode — the one path that can touch a branch at all, and only once both `yolo == "off"` and `approved` are true — refuses to ever create a merge commit ("No rebase, no merge commit, no force" — `src/hoh/delivery.py:16`). The 32 operator merges are `--no-ff` merge commits: a stronger action against the protected branch than the code's own captain-gated path permits itself to perform, executed through a channel (`git merge`, run directly) that `delivery.py`'s guard never sees at all. Exactly one hand-intervention in the same report table carries an explicit "vom Captain ausdrücklich autorisiert" annotation (a one-time, read-only license lookup); the 32 merges carry no comparable annotation, only the operator's own characterisation of the action as within its remit. ⟦merge commit, no force" — `src/hoh/delivery.py:16`). | docs/READINESS.md:63 | A campaign that produced every result file while violating the protocol is FAIL here, because the files are not what is being asked about. * **`export_manifest`** — re-derive it with `python3 tools/export_manifest.py derive`; a count taken against a stale manifest would be a zero that means 'not measured'. * **`export_sync`** — a comparison that did not run is not a green one; the row says so rather than reporting the absence as safe. * **`succession`** — the capsule is not wrong about the past when it drifts -- it is stale about the present, and a successor reading it would be too. * **`identifiers`** — a published tool whose names are in another language is readable only to the people who wrote it. * **`preserve`** — project- and evidence-owned state must not be destroyable by an autonomous run, and the refusal must name the safe operation. * **`self-hosted-topology`** — isolation is not traded for an attribution category; a byte-identical import binds the claim either way. * **`unit-drift`** — the repository's unit is the canonical one; an installed copy is judged against it, never the other way round. * **`durability`** — every registered exit condition re-derives from preserved raw evidence; a stressor marked NOT_RUN is named, not counted. * **`preflight`** — an environment that cannot run the work is not a product failure, and discovering it after the quota is spent is not a measurement. * **`parallelism_baseline`** — the baseline is the premise V3.3 was planned against, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`program_scope`** — a register that is internally consistent can still be a quarter of the programme; only the plan can say it is not. * **`capability_matrix`** — the matrix is what the next phase is planned from, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`build_plan`** — the build order is derived from the register, so it cannot drift from the statuses it is planned against. * **`acceptance`** — an end-to-end acceptance is evidence about one real run; a record that no longer matches that run is not evidence, and a requirement not yet proven is shown, not hidden. * **`programme_checklist`** — the gates this programme runs on are decided by hoh.checklist, so a structurally unsound checklist stops the verdict instead of colouring it. * **`programme_supervisor`** — the P2 gate needs a *current, honest* independent supervisor review of *P2*: every finding other than a severity-consistent NO_ACTION holds the phase open and no decision settles one (O229/G), a record whose stored verdict disagrees with its own findings is not evidence, and the brief the review was performed on must be the one this gate derives for this board. * **`baseline_docs`** — the baselines are summaries of measurements taken elsewhere, so the only thing that can go wrong is being old. * **`attribution`** — the ratio is not a gate -- it is reported so that nobody has to take the phase's own description of itself on trust. * **`paper_audit`** — `coverage` is red on a maintenance item paper/AUDIT.md itself flags and explains: paper/NUMBERS.md catalogues the 2 of a '2 of 3' ratio and not the 3. ⟦* **`succession`** — the capsule is not wrong about the past when it drifts -- it is stale about the present, and a successor reading it would be too.⟧ | a table frame, a provenance line, or the reason a row is advisory; the measurement is in the row itself |

| docs/READINESS.md:64 | A campaign that produced every result file while violating the protocol is FAIL here, because the files are not what is being asked about. * **`export_manifest`** — re-derive it with `python3 tools/export_manifest.py derive`; a count taken against a stale manifest would be a zero that means 'not measured'. * **`export_sync`** — a comparison that did not run is not a green one; the row says so rather than reporting the absence as safe. * **`succession`** — the capsule is not wrong about the past when it drifts -- it is stale about the present, and a successor reading it would be too. * **`identifiers`** — a published tool whose names are in another language is readable only to the people who wrote it. * **`preserve`** — project- and evidence-owned state must not be destroyable by an autonomous run, and the refusal must name the safe operation. * **`self-hosted-topology`** — isolation is not traded for an attribution category; a byte-identical import binds the claim either way. * **`unit-drift`** — the repository's unit is the canonical one; an installed copy is judged against it, never the other way round. * **`durability`** — every registered exit condition re-derives from preserved raw evidence; a stressor marked NOT_RUN is named, not counted. * **`preflight`** — an environment that cannot run the work is not a product failure, and discovering it after the quota is spent is not a measurement. * **`parallelism_baseline`** — the baseline is the premise V3.3 was planned against, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`program_scope`** — a register that is internally consistent can still be a quarter of the programme; only the plan can say it is not. * **`capability_matrix`** — the matrix is what the next phase is planned from, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`build_plan`** — the build order is derived from the register, so it cannot drift from the statuses it is planned against. * **`acceptance`** — an end-to-end acceptance is evidence about one real run; a record that no longer matches that run is not evidence, and a requirement not yet proven is shown, not hidden. * **`programme_checklist`** — the gates this programme runs on are decided by hoh.checklist, so a structurally unsound checklist stops the verdict instead of colouring it. * **`programme_supervisor`** — the P2 gate needs a *current, honest* independent supervisor review of *P2*: every finding other than a severity-consistent NO_ACTION holds the phase open and no decision settles one (O229/G), a record whose stored verdict disagrees with its own findings is not evidence, and the brief the review was performed on must be the one this gate derives for this board. * **`baseline_docs`** — the baselines are summaries of measurements taken elsewhere, so the only thing that can go wrong is being old. * **`attribution`** — the ratio is not a gate -- it is reported so that nobody has to take the phase's own description of itself on trust. * **`paper_audit`** — `coverage` is red on a maintenance item paper/AUDIT.md itself flags and explains: paper/NUMBERS.md catalogues the 2 of a '2 of 3' ratio and not the 3. ⟦* **`identifiers`** — a published tool whose names are in another language is readable only to the people who wrote it.⟧ | a table frame, a provenance line, or the reason a row is advisory; the measurement is in the row itself |

| docs/LIMITATIONS.md:1361 | The first draft carried three paths copied out of a different gate's tolerance list: `CLAIMS.md`, `docs/READINESS.md` and `CLAIMS.json`. The ledger came out after an attack on the guard showed that exempting it would have silently reverted six claims the distribution work added in the public repository -- the defect the file exists to prevent, reintroduced by its own exemption list (O174). An independent review then asked why the other two were exempt at all, and the answer did not survive the question: "generated" describes the content, not the decision, and a file being regenerable says nothing about whether someone added something to it that our regeneration will drop -- which is precisely what happened (O176). The exemption was also unnecessary. ⟦the file exists to prevent, reintroduced by its own exemption list (O174). An⟧ | names internal finding id O174 from DOGFOOD_LEDGER.md, an internal working document this ledger's declared coverage does not extend to, as the finding that the export guard's own exemption list would have reintroduced the defect the guard prevents; the six claims it would have reverted are C-463..C-468 in this ledger |
| docs/READINESS.md:66 | A campaign that produced every result file while violating the protocol is FAIL here, because the files are not what is being asked about. * **`export_manifest`** — re-derive it with `python3 tools/export_manifest.py derive`; a count taken against a stale manifest would be a zero that means 'not measured'. * **`export_sync`** — a comparison that did not run is not a green one; the row says so rather than reporting the absence as safe. * **`succession`** — the capsule is not wrong about the past when it drifts -- it is stale about the present, and a successor reading it would be too. * **`identifiers`** — a published tool whose names are in another language is readable only to the people who wrote it. * **`preserve`** — project- and evidence-owned state must not be destroyable by an autonomous run, and the refusal must name the safe operation. * **`self-hosted-topology`** — isolation is not traded for an attribution category; a byte-identical import binds the claim either way. * **`unit-drift`** — the repository's unit is the canonical one; an installed copy is judged against it, never the other way round. * **`durability`** — every registered exit condition re-derives from preserved raw evidence; a stressor marked NOT_RUN is named, not counted. * **`preflight`** — an environment that cannot run the work is not a product failure, and discovering it after the quota is spent is not a measurement. * **`parallelism_baseline`** — the baseline is the premise V3.3 was planned against, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`program_scope`** — a register that is internally consistent can still be a quarter of the programme; only the plan can say it is not. * **`capability_matrix`** — the matrix is what the next phase is planned from, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`build_plan`** — the build order is derived from the register, so it cannot drift from the statuses it is planned against. * **`acceptance`** — an end-to-end acceptance is evidence about one real run; a record that no longer matches that run is not evidence, and a requirement not yet proven is shown, not hidden. * **`programme_checklist`** — the gates this programme runs on are decided by hoh.checklist, so a structurally unsound checklist stops the verdict instead of colouring it. * **`programme_supervisor`** — the P2 gate needs a *current, honest* independent supervisor review of *P2*: every finding other than a severity-consistent NO_ACTION holds the phase open and no decision settles one (O229/G), a record whose stored verdict disagrees with its own findings is not evidence, and the brief the review was performed on must be the one this gate derives for this board. * **`baseline_docs`** — the baselines are summaries of measurements taken elsewhere, so the only thing that can go wrong is being old. * **`attribution`** — the ratio is not a gate -- it is reported so that nobody has to take the phase's own description of itself on trust. * **`paper_audit`** — `coverage` is red on a maintenance item paper/AUDIT.md itself flags and explains: paper/NUMBERS.md catalogues the 2 of a '2 of 3' ratio and not the 3. ⟦* **`self-hosted-topology`** — isolation is not traded for an attribution category; a byte-identical import binds the claim either way.⟧ | a table frame, a provenance line, or the reason a row is advisory; the measurement is in the row itself |

a stressor marked NOT_RUN is named, not counted. * **`preflight`** — an environment that cannot run the work is not a product failure, and discovering it after the quota is spent is not a measurement. * **`parallelism_baseline`** — the baseline is the premise V3.3 was planned against, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`program_scope`** — a register that is internally consistent can still be a quarter of the programme; only the plan can say it is not. * **`capability_matrix`** — the matrix is what the next phase is planned from, so it is checked rather than remembered. * **`build_plan`** — the build order is derived from the register, so it cannot drift from the statuses it is planned against. * **`acceptance`** — an end-to-end acceptance is evidence about one real run; a record that no longer matches that run is not evidence, and a requirement not yet proven is shown, not hidden. * **`programme_checklist`** — the gates this programme runs on are decided by hoh.checklist, so a structurally unsound checklist stops the verdict instead of colouring it. * **`programme_supervisor`** — the P2 gate needs a *current, honest* independent supervisor review of *P2*: every finding other than a severity-consistent NO_ACTION holds the phase open and no decision settles one (O229/G), a record whose stored verdict disagrees with its own findings is not evidence, and the brief the review was performed on must be the one this gate derives for this board. * **`baseline_docs`** — the baselines are summaries of measurements taken elsewhere, so the only thing that can go wrong is being old. * **`attribution`** — the ratio is not a gate -- it is reported so that nobody has to take the phase's own description of itself on trust. * **`paper_audit`** — `coverage` is red on a maintenance item paper/AUDIT.md itself flags and explains: paper/NUMBERS.md catalogues the 2 of a '2 of 3' ratio and not the 3. ⟦* **`acceptance`** — an end-to-end acceptance is evidence about one real run; | CHANGELOG.md:68 | In the ledger entries O236 to O254, 26 candidates the product had accepted were refused at integration review `[V07t]`. * **Durable programme runtime (P2).** Durable timers, a sentinel, a never-stuck check, session succession with a master epoch, a partial leader lease, a resume loop that acts on due timers, an autonomy contract, a programme checklist bound to the phase gate, and an independent supervisor review of the gate. 26 of P2's 43 registered requirements read PROVEN `[V10c]` `[V10b]`; P2 is not closed. * **Project contract and state ownership.** Read-only `hoh project contract` commands (`schema`, `check`, `impact`, `owner`, `conflicts`) beside `hoh project authority`, `drive` and `handoff`. * **Evidence model.** The `EvidenceClaim` schema and its entry point `tools/evidence_claims.py`; proof classes that keep "built", "tested", "integrated", "behaviourally proven" and "gate satisfied" apart; and an acceptance record that is refused as `STALE` when the code it describes changed after it was taken. * **Programme gate machinery.** Phase gates bound to the register (a gate item that is not bound can no longer read closed), supervisor drift measured against a preserved baseline, each acceptance probe bound to its own register entry, and a union-gate timeout that reports a stable `NOT_RUN` instead of copying an interpreter path into the board. * **Storage lifecycle (operator amendment A1), and its first self-dogfood.** Ownership registry, admission by reservation, durable park and resume under storage pressure, verified archive bundles and targets, host adapters, and `VERIFIED_RELOCATION` with a per-project storage steward -- the only operation that may remove a local copy of project data. ⟦* **Durable programme runtime (P2).** Durable timers, a sentinel, a never-stuck⟧ | carries only identifiers -- phase, requirement, ledger-entry, amendment, stressor or erratum labels, a version, a section sign, a limit number or a figure tag; the figures themselves are bound on their own lines |

| docs/LIMITATIONS.md:100 | Context rollover (Layer A) is merged and has not run live — `hoh project hold`, `rollover`, `rollover-verify` and `rollover-accept` (merge `601168fe`) are tested with fakes; **no live succession has been run, and no P2 row is proven by it** (the one handoff of 2026-10-07 was written by hand before the protocol existed and is not that evidence). The draining states between the freeze and the validated successor are **recorded, not enforced**: nothing refuses `hoh start` or `hoh run` in that window. The first-prompt stall can lose the successor's pointer; the acknowledgement deadline then fails closed (the predecessor stays master) and the pointer is sent again. A capsule's derived facts are only as good as the code that derives them (git, files, run states); a fact nobody derives is not checked, and an operator decision's `decided` status is author-set. **Open follow-up items (tracked HIGH, a prerequisite of the live canary):** the capsule id is not pattern-validated, so an unverified capsule can place its create-only, owner-only acknowledgement file outside the rollover directory; `acquire` is not atomic with the last verification, so a master gap is possible (never two masters); a relative `--root` never rolls over (fail closed); a non-object `--input` raises instead of refusing; `hold --interval` accepts zero or a negative value; nine guard sites have no test that kills their removal. An automatic rotation policy (Layer B) is not built. *Correction by addition, 2026-10-20 (the row stands as written on its date): "no live succession has been run" is no longer true. The build's own rotation policy (`src/hoh/rotation.py`) has requested, and the succession code has completed, live successions of the orchestrating session since 2026-10-11, each recorded by a `rotation_finished` row; the README front gives the counts and the method. That log is the build's working record and is not exported. The correction changes no P2 row, and the other limits of this row are unchanged.* — ledger O255; `src/hoh/rollover.py`, `src/hoh/succession_capsule.py` | carries only identifiers -- phase, requirement, ledger-entry, amendment, stressor or erratum labels, a version, a section sign, a limit number or a figure tag; the figures themselves are bound on their own lines |

| CHANGELOG.md:97 | This release has no README section for it yet, because that section would state what a session does, and no smoke has shown it. * **Owned control of the agents HoH starts (P2-17; merges `33491c6e` and `a7d73b8e`).** An `AgentControlAdapter` sits between the dispatcher and Herdr, and the dispatcher spells no Herdr command itself any more. Every agent HoH creates is registered in an append-only `owned-agents.jsonl` bound to the run that wrote it; every acting verb on an id the registry does not hold is refused before Herdr is called; `close_tab` is refused unless the runtime's snapshot shows the tab and every pane in it as owned, and fails closed on a malformed snapshot. P2-17 reads **PROVEN, with limits stated in the register and in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`**: the `program` scope of a role is built by two tests only (the type's own and the registry test that adopts one) and no product path starts a program-scope agent through the registry; the registry is a record kept by HoH's own process, not a defence against a process of the same user that can write the run directory; `close_tab` ignores the tab's pane count, so it relies on the runtime's snapshot listing every pane of the tab; a pane that was never released stays owned on disk, and after a Herdr restart a recalled id may name a pane that is not ours; restart recall needs the registry directory's name to equal the run id, which the benchmark's arm A layout does not give (it recalls nothing and fails safe). **Not run: a live `hoh run` and a restored-pane adoption against a real Herdr server.** * **Disk-full-safe durable writes, two more slices (P2-41; merges `ae235948` and `e3390276`).** Amendments, role approval files, governance records, the restore command, the run records, the integrity close and the launcher's prepare step now write through the durable-write primitives and stay fail-closed under injected ENOSPC and partial writes. ⟦malformed snapshot. Every agent HoH creates is registered in an append-only `owned-agents.jsonl` bound to the run that wrote it; every acting verb on an id the registry does not hold is refused before Herdr is called; `close_tab` is refused unless the runtime's snapshot shows the tab and every pane in it as owned, and fails closed on a malformed snapshot. P2-17 reads **PROVEN, with limits stated in the register and in `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`**: the `program` scope of a role is built by two tests only (the type's own and the registry test that adopts one) and no product path starts a program-scope agent through the registry; the registry is a record kept by HoH's own process, not a defence against a process of the same user that can write the run directory; `close_tab` ignores the tab's pane count, so it relies on the runtime's snapshot listing every pane of the tab; a pane that was never released stays owned on disk, and after a Herdr restart a recalled id may name a pane that is not ours; restart recall needs the registry directory's name to equal the run id, which the benchmark's arm A layout does not give (it recalls nothing and fails safe). **Not run: a live `hoh run` and a restored-pane adoption against a real Herdr server.** * **Disk-full-safe durable writes, two more slices (P2-41; merges `ae235948` and `e3390276`).** Amendments, role approval files, governance records, the restore command, the run records, the integrity close and the launcher's prepare step now write through the durable-write primitives and stay fail-closed under injected ENOSPC and partial writes. ⟦malformed snapshot. | CHANGELOG.md:277 | The lift of P2-42 rests on one run of one registered project on one host with the Claude role harness only; the approval-resume of a registered run and the refusal paths were not exercised live. The rotation of the orchestrating session has the limits of the third alpha: one project on one host; the expiry, withdrawal and error paths not exercised live; the item-level rotation without a caller outside the tests; the capsule input derived by the orchestrating session's script before each rotation, not by the product. * **The test suite at R, and the nodes the closure turns red by design.** Two measurements of the full suite exist at R and differ: the orchestrating session's run and the board's `tests` row, taken between the passes of the regeneration with the tree dirty in record paths; both are recorded in the closure record with the cause of each named failure, neither is re-run for this release, and which nodes the board's extra failures are is left open there. Six test nodes pin "unmet" for the P2 exit and turn red at the commit at which the exit turns; a test change is not a record path and would break the succession window, so they are re-stated to the closed state as the first test change after the tag. One test of the program scope builds the scope from the plan without the operator amendments and fails at every commit of this period while the scope check with amendments reads COMPLETE; it is brought to the amendments after the tag. * **The board.** The rows that do not read PASS at the sealing commit, with the reasons the board gives: the test suite and the union invariants (the full suite at R in the real repository read 7082 passed, 4 failed, 2 skipped, with the cause of each failure named in the closure record; the board's own `tests` row, taken between the passes of the regeneration, read 7078 passed, 8 failed at the sealing commit and 7079 passed, 7 failed at the figures commit after X; records entries O267 and O268); the benchmark freeze, which reads DRIFTED because files moved after the freeze and the later modules are not named in its artefact, and both benchmark rows with it (one advisory); the export manifest, which was out of date at S, X and the commit after X by design and is re-derived in this commit; the export sync, which has no export checkout set; the succession row as it stood before the capsule commit, re-measured after X; the consistency check, which reads the working tree against the base of the figures table and is re-rendered in this commit; and the external CI, whose recorded run tested a different export. ⟦there. That is a fence, not isolation. It is merged on the development line after `v0.3.0` and is in no release before `v0.4.0a1`. - **Pre-authorised external acts.** The bounded executor (`src/hoh/extexec.py`) carries out an external act that a contract pre-authorised, and only narrowly: a target the contract names, within the pre-authorised number counted durably before the act, with create-only, digest-bound records; every release and publish class is refused whatever the contract says, the programme stop is honoured, and everything else stays with a person.
